hs-hermitian-lattice: A Hermitian space is encoded by a K-basis b of V indexed by a finite type and, for each infinite place v, an invertible complex matrix X_v (Formalism.BasicNotions.HLat bundles b, X and a submodule L). The norm at v is the standard norm of X_v^{-1} applied to the b-coordinates of x embedded by v.embedding, Mathlib's chosen embedding in the place; every positive definite Hermitian form on V_v arises in this way. Formalism.HermitianLatticesTheory.realize sends x to the real and imaginary parts of these coordinates at all places, so that its squared norm is the sum over v of the squared norms at v. Lattices are arbitrary O_K-submodules, finitely generated where a statement asks for it. Formalism.HN.dualLat is {f : f(A) in O_K} and Formalism.HN.dualFrame replaces X_v by the inverse transpose, which gives the dual norm. Formalism.HN.htMap is (1/r) times the sum over v of log of the squared operator norms Formalism.HN.opNormAt. The statements also carry a StarRing instance on K, which none of these definitions uses.
hs-slopes: The Lean defines covolume, degree (-log covol), rank and slope for Z-submodules of a Euclidean space (Formalism.F) and applies them to the realization of an O_K-submodule. Formalism.HN.muDef is 2 slope - log 2 + log|d_K|/[K:Q], which is the mu of the text (Remark hs-normalization); muMaxDef and muMinDef apply the same affine change to muMax and muMin, the sSup over nonzero O_K-submodules and the sInf over saturated proper O_K-submodules of the slopes of the orthogonal projections. Formalism.HN.hnStep is the sSup of the nonzero submodules N with theta <= muMin N, in Z-slope units: the A^{>= theta} of the text is hnStep at (theta + log 2 - log|d_K|/[K:Q])/2. Formalism.HN.slopeList has one entry for each unit of Z-rank, so each Harder-Narasimhan slope of the text occurs [K:Q] times there. The text defines slopes only for nonzero lattices; the Lean values for the zero module (sSup and sInf of the empty set are 0) are never used in this chapter.
hs-normalization: In the Lean, mu is defined by the second formula (muDef). Formalism.HN.size_maximal_slope relates it to ht = 2^{rn}|d_K|^{-n/2} covol, which is exp(-deg A) in the notation of the text; this gives the first formula. The comparison with Bost's conventions is made only in the text.
hs-hn-polygon: Standard; the same as the existence and basic properties of the Harder-Narasimhan filtration (Stuhler, Grayson), in the formulation by thresholds. The Lean proves them for any ring R, R-module V and additive map rho from V to a Euclidean space that is injective and discrete on L (IsLat), with slopes taken over R-submodules; with R = O_K and rho = realize this is the statement for Hermitian lattices (Formalism.HN.place_lattice_structure shows that the realization is discrete of Z-rank [K:Q] rk). Part (1) is MuChar (Formalism.HN.muChar), part (2) is HNStep (Formalism.HN.hnStep_spec), part (3) is HNSlopes (Formalism.HN.hnSlopes), which also gives the polygon bound deg N <= hnPoly(rk N), and part (4) is HNExtreme (Formalism.HN.polygon_extreme_slopes) together with the monotonicity in (3). The counts in the Lean are in Z-rank, [K:Q] times those of the text.
hs-bost-slope-inequality: The same as Bost's slope inequality (Bost 2001, Proposition 4.5; Bost 2020, Proposition 1.4.1) in the normalization of Remark hs-normalization, for archimedean heights only: since phi(A) lies in the target lattice, the finite part of Bost's height is at most 0 and is dropped. The Lean derives Formalism.HN.slope_inequality_mean from a version for Euclidean lattices with one Lipschitz constant C (Formalism.HN.slope_inequality_general), after rescaling the metric of W at each place v by ||phi_v|| e^{-h/2}; the rescaled metric has the same slopes (Formalism.HN.twist_of, from rescale_covolume_formula) and all its operator norms equal e^{h/2}.
hs-almost-tight-frame: The Lean states the two conditions for complex matrices B_i with rows indexed by a finite type alpha and columns by iota_i (FrameDeviationLinear, FrameTraceRatioLinear), with F_i = frK c_i B_i, Q = frQ c B and the squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm hs2; the same conditions appear unbundled in Formalism.HN.FrameLA1 and Formalism.HN.TheoremF. The second condition is written tr(Q^2) <= (1+eta)(tr Q)^2 / dim E, which is equivalent for dim E >= 1 and holds trivially for E = 0. The text writes the conditions for linear maps between inner product spaces; the matrices are these maps in orthonormal bases.
hs-frame-complement: Faithful (Formalism.HN.FrameLA1). The proof follows frame_linear_algebra_first: fam_bound is inequality (b), sum_re_inner_bound is (a), W_upper is the Bessel step, and final_real1 is the conclusion. A statement FrameLA with the weaker constant 2 eta also exists (Formalism/CorankShare/StatementFR.lean); the version used is FrameLA1.
hs-near-orthogonal: InputSG, for matrices B_i with rows indexed by alpha and columns by iota_i: the off-diagonal blocks are KpG = sqrt(gamma_i gamma_j) B_i^* B_j, whose squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm is gamma_i gamma_j ||B_i^* B_j||^2 for gamma >= 0, and the diagonal blocks are KdG = gamma_i B_i^* B_i. Chapter integral-structure calls these conditions, with the provisos on the dimensions, the orthogonality link (LinkS).
hs-near-orthogonal-frame: Formalism.LFunctionChainParameters.MatrixLatticeEstimates.ramification_linear_case_holds (RamLin): the compressed maps are the matrix products Bf_i Vr_i with Vr_i^* Vr_i = 1. Its proof transfers to Fin-indexed matrices and combines compressTraceSquareBound (the second frame condition: cor_common for the bounds on Q, compressTraceLowerBound and ram_gap for the trace lost by compression, and num_main, num_ram and num_step for the arithmetic) with compressDiagDefectBound (the first frame condition). The two elementary inequalities of the proof are num_main and num_ram. The Lean names refer to the compression to the ramified subspace in the application.
hs-share: Formalism.HN.thmF_share, which reduces to frameB_share for u > 0. The Lean indexes the numbers by pairs (i, j) with j < m_i; the text uses one finite index set. For u = tau = 0 the Lean reads u/(u+tau) as 0/0 = 0, which is the convention of the text.
hs-layer-cake: Formalism.CorankShareLayerCake.FR.layer_cake_formula (LayerCake), with the x_j indexed by Fin n and interval integrability of min(1, w) on [0, H] as a hypothesis.
hs-frame-situation: Bundled in the Lean as LatGeom (the lattices, the maps, the heights, the place v, the frame matrices and delta) and LatNum (s, u, H); Formalism.HN.TheoremF and TheoremFSharp take the same hypotheses unbundled. The inner products at v are given by invertible matrices Y_i and Y', whose columns are orthonormal bases in the coordinates of b_i and b'; they are unrelated to the metrics X_i and X'. The maps tilde B_i are matrices Ball_i with rows indexed by kappa + kappa_1, of size dim W + l, whose kappa-block is Y'^{-1} (matrix of B_i at v) Y_i; the kappa_1-rows are arbitrary. The text requires every V_i to be nonzero, a special case: the Lean requires only that the sum of the d_i be positive, and for a zero N_i its condition mu_max(N_i) - h_i <= s + u is read with the Lean value of mu_max of the zero module.
hs-frame-slope-inequality-sharp: Formalism.HN.TheoremFSharp, proved as theoremFSharp_of frame_linear_algebra_first. Step 0 is hD; Step 1 is hcor (via thmF_share and frameB_count_lt); Step 2 is hMle (via slope_inequality_mean and the HNStep property frameB_hnStep); Step 3 is thmF_place and hplace; Step 4 is hcnt, hlow, layer_cake_formula and frameB_integral. The Lean works with Z-slopes and converts with frameB_muDef, frameB_muMaxDef and frameB_muMinDef; its counts are [K:Q] times those of the text. The plan's paraphrase asked for 0 <= s - mu_min(C) <= H and for orthonormal coordinates; the Lean asks for s - mu_min(C) <= H with H >= 0, and the coordinates at v are arbitrary. The plan listed only the weaker form with log|I| (Corollary hs-frame-slope-inequality); this sharp form is also proved and is the one from which that form is derived.
hs-frame-slope-inequality: Formalism.HN.TheoremF, proved as theoremF_of_sharp: the term log|I| is subtracted from the sharp bound using log|I| >= 0, so it is slack. This is the form used by flat_lattice_theorem_holds and hence by Frame_at.
hs-comparison-with-bost: Not in the Lean. The bound from Bost's inequality alone, the example of an orthogonal sum and the reformulation through duality are standard consequences, argued briefly in the remark itself.
hs-frame-from-near-orthogonality: Formalism.LFunctionChainParameters.MatrixLatticeEstimates.ramification_condition_holds gives both bounds; joint_a_ramified_holds (JointARam) is its first part, the one used by frame_at_of. The isometric embeddings nu_i are matrices Vr_i with Vr_i^* Vr_i = 1, the maps hat B_i are matrices Bf_i, and tilde B_i = Ball_i = Bf_i Vr_i.
hs-frame-realisation: Formalism.MainNotions.Lnk.FrameReal_at D sigma delta_e e_B. The coefficient field is D.what2.LL, the words D.what2.Word, the row deficit delta = D.what2.delp, D^* = D.what2.Dstar, the division datum D.div (RR, Nu, Bk, h), and dim M_u = D.duS u, the complex dimension of (D.mem u).A.Mu0. Conditions (1)-(3) are LatGeom for the dual basis, dual metrics and dual lattice of RR (dualB, dualX, dualL), which also lists the invertibility of the metric matrices; (3) is Ball_u = Bf_u Vr_u together with the kappa-block condition of LatGeom; the condition card(iota_f u) = D.duS u says dim F_u = dim M_u.
hs-frame-bound: Formalism.MainNotions.Lnk.Frame_at D eta_B e_B, with s_D = sFrame and u_D = uFrame. The Lean definition has no hypothesis that CC and the N_u are nonzero and finitely generated; it then uses the Lean values of slopes of arbitrary submodules, of division by zero (so (1 - delta)^{-1} = 0 when delta = 1) and of logarithms of nonpositive numbers (Real.log x = log|x|), which matter only if a rank vanishes, delta = 1 or u_D < 0. The text adds the hypothesis so that the slopes are those of Definition hs-slopes; under the hypotheses of Proposition hs-frame-at-glued-lattice it holds, delta < 1 and u_D >= 0.
hs-frame-at-glued-lattice: Formalism.MainNotions.Lnk.frame_at_of. The size data (Definition pd-size-data) are L : SizeData2 D, used only through its scale x = L.sc.x > 1 and Gamma = GamL L = exp(L.CGam m^5 f L.sc.L), where L.sc.L = x^eps. Hypotheses (2) and (3) are ChProviso_at L C0 and ChCode_at L C0 C_H, (4) is D.NuFull, and (5) is Lat_at D. The proof does not use the upper bound in (2) or the clause mu_min(CC) = -mu_max(RR) of (5). In the Lean, eta = 5 sigma + 3 sqrt(delta_e) and e = 2 e_0, as in the text. The argument that CC is nonzero is needed only for the hypothesis that the text adds to Definition hs-frame-bound. Chapter period-divisibility does not list the constant C_Gamma (L.CGam, with L.Gam_eq relating it to the members' Gamma_P) among the size data; Definition pd-size-data should include it.
